comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DIAGNOSTIC STATE — plan PASSED first round (0 blocking, 1 advisory), SIGNED at 44d9250ea, CLAIMED. Recording the trace so far so the next session starts from data, not from scratch.

**BOTH HALVES OF THE PLUMBING LOOK CORRECT IN ISOLATION — that is the puzzle, and it is why the plan forbids assuming the `gate_config` omission is the cause.**
* AGENT steps: `workflow/runs.py:144-156` `RunnerAgentStep.run` does
    cfg = self._config or LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=self._repo_root)
    cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model(cfg, step=ctx.step.get('model'), workflow=ctx.workflow.get('model')))
  and the code-review dispatch DOES pass `config=cfg` into `RunnerAgentStep`. So a prompt step's
  `model:` is read and resolved — on this path.
* BATCH steps: `code_review/batch_runner.py:60-61,83-84` resolves `req.model_ladder[0]` via
  `resolve_model_string` and sets `step['model'] = model`. Also correct — on this path.
* The doc is NOT transformed: `_assemble_code_review_run` does a plain `doc = _gate_doc("code-review", repo_root)`, and the package demonstrably loads the worktree file with all five declarations.

**WHY THE LIVE LOG CANNOT SETTLE WHICH PATH RAN — a real limitation of the instrument.** `usage_log.record(op=...)` records the PROMPT NAME, not the step id. `code-review-base` is the prompt used BOTH by the `base` step AND as the `batch:` finder for `round_a`/`round_b`, so the nine observed ops cannot be attributed to steps. `code-review-docs` / `-tests` / `-deletion-impact` / `-project-review-phase-boundaries` / `-api-compat` are criteria overlays, i.e. batch work; `code-review-verify` and `code-review-coach` look like agent steps. But 'looks like' is not attribution, and attributing them by name would repeat the reasoning error that has already cost this epic three false starts.

**THEREFORE THE RECORDING-RUNNER TEST IS THE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT JUST THE REGRESSION GUARD.** It observes (step_id -> model handed to the runner) directly, which is the one fact neither the usage log nor source reading has produced. Write it FIRST, confirm RED, and let it name the broken seam — then fix exactly that.

CONFIRMED FACTS to build on (all independently verified): the defect is real and pre-existing (nine calls all on `cfg.model`, including `verify`'s 172e-era `model: standard`); H2 (config not loaded) and H3 (class table falling back to built-in defaults) are both ELIMINATED — H3 because `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS['standard']` is sonnet and `verify` ran on OPUS; and the asymmetry lead stands — plan-review wraps `gate_config(cfg)` (gate_dispatch ~:146-163) and code-review does not (~:414-424), while plan-review demonstrably honours classes (41/1 opus/sonnet observed live across two providers).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
STEP 0 DESIGN DECISION, MEASURED — the plan requires picking one threading mechanism and recording why. Plan PASSED round 5 (0 blocking, 3 advisory) after R2/R3/R4; re-signed and certified at 44d9250ea.

**CHOSEN: (c) a ContextVar set by the step executor, read at `runner.py:547`.** Both the step id AND the raw declared class token ride on it.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED IT: **`RunRequest` is constructed at 25 sites under `src/rebar`** — spec_scan.py:123, enrich.py:81, operations.py:177, eval_solver.py:164 and :233, xcheck.py:199 and :337, prerequisites.py:228, plan_review/__init__.py:164, and more. Most have NO step context at all (a spec scan and an enrich pass are not workflow steps).
* (a) a new `RunRequest` field — rejected on that count. Required would churn all 25; optional would leave ~24 sites passing `None` forever, which is noise that makes the field look meaningless at every site that legitimately has no step.
* (b) overloading the existing `target: dict` — rejected: `target` means the thing under review, not the caller. Reusing it would save a field and cost a reader's understanding of both.
* (c) ContextVar — zero churn at all 25 sites, and it scopes naturally: the executor sets it around one step's execution and drops it after, so a call made OUTSIDE a step simply has no step id, which is the truthful answer rather than a placeholder. **Direct in-repo precedent:** `_active_gate_config` (`llm/config.py:88`), whose own comment says it mirrors "the active read-root ContextVars in `rebar.llm.gate_context`". So this is the established way this codebase threads run-scoped context to a deep chokepoint.

WHAT `record()` GAINS (additive, following its existing `if model:` pattern so absent values are simply omitted rather than written as null): `step` and `model_class`. `model_class` is written ONLY when the raw declared token is one of `CLASS_NAMES` — a literal model id is not a class, and recording it as one would recreate the ambiguity Step 0 exists to remove.

NEXT: held-out TDD — write the attribution test FIRST, confirm RED for the right reason, then implement. The test must assert on a log produced by an actual gate run (per the AC), not on `usage_log.py`'s source, because reading the writer cannot show that the step id ARRIVES.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
TWO MORE HYPOTHESES ELIMINATED, and one CONSTRAINT ON THE TEST DESIGN discovered. Both cheap, both recorded so the search keeps narrowing instead of circling.

**ELIMINATED — the v3 migration strips the declarations.** The offline harness (`tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_workflow.py:402`) runs the gate through `migrate.migrate_to_current(yaml.safe_load(gate))` before execution, so a migration that dropped or relocated `model:` would explain everything. VERIFIED it does not: before and after migration the doc is identical — base `model=frontier`; round_a/round_b `model_ladder=['frontier']`; verify/coach `model=standard`. So the declarations survive YAML -> migrate -> doc intact.

**CONSTRAINT ON THE END-TO-END TEST — this changes how AC 'recording runner' must be built.** The existing offline harness passes `agent_runner=_FakeRunner(...)`, which REPLACES `RunnerAgentStep` wholesale. So a naive recording runner in that style would observe `ctx.step['model']` (the declared token delivered by the engine) but would NEVER exercise `RunnerAgentStep`'s `resolve_model(cfg, step=ctx.step.get('model'), ...)` — the exact line whose behaviour is in question. A test built that way would pass while proving only what 3768's tests already proved.
=> the recording seam must sit BENEATH `RunnerAgentStep`, not instead of it: keep the production agent step and inject a fake UNDERLYING runner that captures the `cfg.model` it is handed. That observes the post-resolution value, which is the fact at issue. Write it that way, and confirm RED.

REMAINING SUSPECT, stated as a suspect and not a conclusion: `config.py:211` is `return resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model)` — it passes NO `repo_root`, so the class table is loaded from the ambient root. The live code-review run executes inside `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)`, which redirects reads to a snapshot. Whether that redirect changes what the class table resolves to is UNVERIFIED — and note it cannot be the whole story, because a fallback class table would still give `verify` (declaring `standard`) a SONNET model, and the live log showed OPUS. Step 0's per-step attribution is what settles this; do not act on this suspicion before then.

CUMULATIVE ELIMINATIONS on this defect: config-not-loaded (H2), class-table-fallback (H3), migration-strips-declarations, doc-not-my-copy, review_code-does-not-run-the-gate. All ruled out by experiment.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
**THE TEST'S CAPTURE POINT, located precisely — and it independently justifies Step 0's ContextVar.**

`RunnerAgentStep.run` resolves the model and then, at `runs.py:236`, does
    runner = get_runner(cfg, override=self._runner)
and at `:261`
    outs.append(runner.run(req))
where `cfg` is the copy carrying the RESOLVED model and `req.config` is that cfg. So constructing `RunnerAgentStep(runner=<fake>, repo_root=..., config=cfg)` makes `get_runner` return the fake via its `override=` parameter, and the fake's `run(req)` receives **`req.config.model` — the POST-resolution value**. That is the fact in question, observed at the production seam rather than around it.

**AND HERE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR THE DESIGN: the fake CANNOT attribute that model to a step either.** `RunRequest` carries `system_prompt`, `instructions`, `config`, `reviewers`, `target`, `langfuse_prompt` — no step id. The prompt id would separate `verify` (`code-review-verify`) from `coach` (`code-review-coach`), but NOT `base` from the `round_a`/`round_b` batch finder, because all three use the prompt `code-review-base`. That is the SAME ambiguity that makes the live usage log unattributable.
So the test and the production log need the SAME missing fact, which is independent confirmation that Step 0 is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: the ContextVar carrying (step id, declared token) is what lets BOTH the fake runner and `usage_log.record()` attribute a call to a step. Implement Step 0 first, then the test consumes it — the test exercising the observability it depends on is a feature here, not circularity, because the ContextVar's own contract is asserted separately (set/read, and inert when unset).

IMPLEMENTATION ORDER, now fully determined:
1. ContextVar in the step executor: set (step id, raw declared `model:`/`model_ladder[0]`) around each step's execution; drop on exit. Precedent: `_active_gate_config` (`llm/config.py:88`).
2. `usage_log.record()` gains `step` + `model_class` (written only when the token is in `CLASS_NAMES`), additive, following the existing `if model:` omission pattern.
3. `runner.py:547` passes both through from the ContextVar.
4. THE RED TEST at the seam above: real `RunnerAgentStep`, fake underlying runner via `override=`, assert per-step `req.config.model` equals the declared class's resolved model under a class table whose values differ from `cfg.model`. Confirm RED before step 1 lands, since today it will report `cfg.model` for every step.
5. Re-run the live probe; the per-step attribution then names the broken seam directly.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN BY EXPERIMENT — and it is NOT in any of the three suspected seams ═══

**`PydanticAIRunner.run` DISCARDS `req.config` and resolves the model from the config it was
CONSTRUCTED with.** `runner.py:239` is `cfg = self._config`, and `runner.py:283` is
`resolved = _pai_model(cfg)`. So the per-step model that `RunnerAgentStep` carefully computes into
`req.config.model` is never consulted; every call in a gate run uses the single config baked at
gate-dispatch time (`gate_dispatch.py:411` `runner_sel = request.runner or get_runner(cfg)`).

THE EXPERIMENT (direct, decisive, no LLM spend): construct `PydanticAIRunner(cfg(model=
"CONSTRUCTOR-MODEL"))`, call `run(RunRequest(config=cfg(model="PER-STEP-MODEL")))` inside a gate
session, and spy on `_pai_model`. Result: `req.config.model == "PER-STEP-MODEL"` while the model
handed to `_pai_model` is `"CONSTRUCTOR-MODEL"`. The declaration is computed correctly and then
thrown away one layer below where anyone had looked.

**THIS EXPLAINS EVERY OBSERVATION, including the one that looked contradictory.** Nine live calls
all on cfg.model; `verify`'s `model: standard` among them; pre-existing rather than a 3768
regression; and both halves of the plumbing "correct in isolation" — because they ARE correct. The
defect is downstream of both.

**A PREVIOUSLY-ELIMINATED HYPOTHESIS WAS ELIMINATED ON FAULTY REASONING — recording the correction
because it is what kept the search away from this seam for three sessions.** H3 (class-table
fallback) was dismissed with "an empty table gives `standard` → SONNET, but the log showed OPUS".
Two things were missed:
 1. `_parse_slot` (`model_classes.py:158`) is
    `model = raw.get("model") or fallback_default or _DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]`, where
    `fallback_default` is the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`. With that env var set, an
    UNCONFIGURED class resolves to it for ALL THREE classes — so "empty table ⇒ sonnet" is only
    true when `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is unset. (Measured here: it IS unset on this host, so this is not
    the live mechanism — but the inference was unsound regardless.)
 2. **MEASURED, and it reframes the whole live probe: this repo configures NO `model_classes`
    table at all** (`_read_llm_file_table(None)` returns `{}`), so the built-in defaults apply and
    `frontier` → `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` — which IS `cfg.model` (`DEFAULT_MODEL` is
    `claude-opus-4-8`). Therefore `base`, `round_a` and `round_b` (all declaring `frontier`) are
    EXPECTED to run on opus, honoured or not. Those calls carried no information. The ONLY
    discriminating steps in the whole gate are `verify` and `coach`, which declare `standard`
    (→ sonnet). "Nine of nine on opus" was six-plus uninformative rows plus two real ones.

**THE OFFLINE TEST I WROTE IS GREEN, AND THAT IS ALSO A FINDING, NOT A FAILURE.**
`tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_step_model_attribution.py` runs the REAL gate doc through the
real interpreter with the production `RunnerAgentStep` and a fake runner beneath it (the b690
capture point: `req.config.model` at `runner.run(req)`), under a class table whose three values
differ from `cfg.model`. All seven assertions pass, and a mutation check
(`resolve_model(cfg, step=None, workflow=None)`) turns five of them red naming all five steps — so
the test is sound and capable, and it PROVES the interpreter → `RunnerAgentStep` → `resolve_model`
→ `CodeReviewBatchRunner` chain is correct. The capture point named in this ticket's earlier
comment is one layer too high to see the actual defect: it observes the value the runner is
handed, and the bug is that the runner ignores what it is handed. Keeping that test (it pins the
upper half) and adding one BENEATH the model resolution.

**SCOPE WIDENS, AND THIS NEEDS A DECISION.** The defect is in the shared runner, not in
code-review, so it affects EVERY workflow that declares a per-step model — plan-review and the
completion gate too. That also retires the "asymmetry lead": plan-review only LOOKED like it
honoured classes because with no class table `frontier` == `cfg.model` == opus, so its 41/1
opus/sonnet split is explained without `gate_config` having anything to do with it. Next: design
the fix at `runner.py`, which is OUTSIDE the three files step 5 anticipated
(gate_dispatch/runs/batch_runner) — checking the plan's Scope and file_impact before editing, since
a fix landing in an unpinned file is exactly the kind of plan/implementation divergence the review
gate blocks on.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ FIXED, RED→GREEN, and the fix follows a contract the codebase had already written down ═══

**THE FIX (one line + a documented helper), `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`:**
`run()` opened with `cfg = self._config`; it now opens with `cfg = _effective_config(self._config,
req)`, which returns the runner's config with `req.config.model` substituted when the request
carries a different one (and returns the floor object UNCHANGED otherwise).

**WHY THIS SHAPE, AND WHY IT IS NOT AN INVENTION.** `structured_run.build_usage_limits` already
states the rule verbatim — "`self._config` (`cfg`) is the floor; `req.config` is the per-call
override" — added under bug 59bc precisely so a finding-rich Pass-2 verifier could raise its own
step budget "without a shared runner's `self._config` changing under other steps". `temperature`
follows the same rule at `runner.py:416`. The MODEL was the one per-call value that did not, so this
is bringing an outlier into line with an existing documented contract rather than adding a new
mechanism.

Two deliberate details:
* **Substituted into a COPY of the config, not read as a loose variable at the resolution point.**
  Everything model-adjacent downstream reads `cfg` — the `ProviderSession`, `capabilities_for`, the
  fallback chain, `cache_settings_for`, `base_url` — so substituting into the config keeps all of
  them consistent with the model that actually runs. Reading a separate `model` variable at
  `_pai_model` only would have left the provider session built for the FLOOR's provider, which is
  exactly the cross-provider incoherence this epic exists to remove.
* **A copy, so honouring one step cannot change the floor for the next.** The runner instance is
  shared across every step of a gate run; there is a test for this specific leak.

**RED FIRST, CONFIRMED, AND FOR THE RIGHT REASON.** New `tests/unit/test_llm_model_per_request.py`
(sibling to `test_llm_temperature.py`, the same per-call-override family) spies `_pai_model` — the
resolution point, i.e. BENEATH where the value is handed in — and delegates to the real function so
the run completes. Pre-fix: 2 failed, 1 passed, both failures showing `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`
(the runner's own cfg) where the request asked for `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. The passing one is
the CONTROL (request and runner agree ⇒ unchanged), so the failures cannot be "no model reached the
resolver". Post-fix: 3/3 green. Third test pins the no-leak property: two sequential `run()` calls,
the first with an override, must resolve `[sonnet, opus]` — pre-fix it resolved `[opus, opus]`.

**THE ORIGINAL REPORT, REPLICATED AS RESOLVED.** The same experiment that proved the defect now
prints `model handed to _pai_model = ['PER-STEP-MODEL']` against `req.config.model =
'PER-STEP-MODEL'`. Before the fix it printed `['CONSTRUCTOR-MODEL']`.

**ON THE CAPTURE-POINT AC — stating this plainly rather than claiming the AC as written.** The plan
asks for ONE offline end-to-end test observed RED pre-fix. What exists instead is a two-part guard,
and the split is forced by where the defect turned out to be:
 * `tests/unit/workflow/test_code_review_step_model_attribution.py` — real gate doc, real
   interpreter, real `RunnerAgentStep`, fake runner beneath it; asserts all five steps
   (`base`/`round_a`/`round_b`/`verify`/`coach`) receive their declared class and that none falls
   through to `cfg.model`. GREEN both before and after, because the upper half was never broken.
   Mutation-checked (`step=None, workflow=None` ⇒ 5 failures naming all five steps), so it is
   capable, not vacuous.
 * `tests/unit/test_llm_model_per_request.py` — the runner layer, RED pre-fix as above.
Composed they cover the whole chain, but no single test yet observes five-steps-by-declaration
BENEATH the runner. Building that one next (a real `PydanticAIRunner` with a `FunctionModel`
override driving the real gate, with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` enabled), because it is also what ACs 1-3
need — the usage-log attribution must be asserted from a log an actual gate run produced, not from
reading `usage_log.py`. One harness serves both.

**AND A HONEST NOTE ON THE FIRST [operator-attested] CRITERION.** It asks for the live probe to be
RE-RUN on the broken code so the per-step attribution names the seam. That did not happen and now
cannot: the seam was named by a deterministic local experiment (spy `_pai_model`, compare against
`req.config.model`) that is strictly stronger than a live probe — it isolates the mechanism, costs
no tokens, and is replayable — and the code is now fixed. Step 0's attribution IS built and is what
the new end-to-end test asserts against. Flagging for the operator rather than quietly treating the
criterion as met by a different artifact.

**SCOPE NOTE for the record:** the fix landed in `runner.py`, which is in this ticket's Scope and
`file_impact` but was described there as the `usage_log.record` call site; the Scope's "expect to
change ONE of these" list (gate_dispatch / runs / batch_runner) named three files and the answer was
in none of them. The plan anticipated the uncertainty ("the seam is NOT yet identified, and Step 0
exists to identify it") but its enumeration was a prediction that the data falsified. Recording the
divergence rather than letting the plan read as if it had called it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ THE SAME ROOT CAUSE WAS BREAKING FOUR MORE PER-CALL MODEL CHOICES, ALL IN PLAN-REVIEW ═══

Committed as **2e17171e5c** (`b690: honour a step's declared model at the runner`), Change-Id
`Id942221c950b8c38eb09295d634cb0a37f581653`, on top of 44d9250ea. NOT pushed yet — full unit suite
re-running first. Then I audited the blast radius of the fix, and it is wider than this ticket's
title. Recording it because it changes gate behaviour and the operator should decide, not me.

**MEASURED: of 22 `RunRequest` construction sites under `src/rebar`, FOUR deliberately pass a
config DIFFERENT from the one their runner was built with — and all four were therefore silently
ineffective.** Every one is in plan-review:
 * `plan_review/xcheck.py:199` (contradiction sub-call) — `runner_sel = runner or get_runner(cfg)`
   then `config=_verifier_cfg(cfg)`.
 * `plan_review/xcheck.py:337` (comment-trail sub-call) — same shape.
 * `plan_review/__init__.py:164` (novelty sub-call) — `config=replace(_verifier_cfg(cfg),
   temperature=0.0)`.
 * `plan_review/prerequisites.py:228` — `call_cfg = dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=model)`.

So `_verifier_cfg` — the whole point of `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`, "a focused yes/no verification is
a decisive, non-open-ended judgement, so a cheaper/faster model is sufficient" — has been building a
verifier config that the runner then ignored. Three Pass-2 sub-calls that were meant to run on the
cheaper decisive model have in fact been running on the frontier model.

**AND THE FOURTH IS WORSE THAN A MISSED OPTIMISATION — IT MADE A PROVENANCE RECORD UNTRUE.**
`prerequisites.py` implements a SIZE-ESCALATION LADDER: on a context-limit error it retries a bin on
a higher model (`ladder = sizing.models_at_or_above(model)`), and records the producing model per id
via `_from(model, …)`. Its own comment at `:202-204` states the requirement:

    # A ladder escalation re-runs a bin on a HIGHER model, so the producing model is not always
    # cfg.model; emit_indeterminate must report what actually ran, not what was configured
    # (client report §4).

Both halves of that were broken by the same discard. The escalation never escalated — every rung ran
on `cfg.model` — and the record reported the model the code ASKED for rather than the one that ran,
which is precisely the failure that comment exists to prevent. A client report (§4) is behind it.

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX: it is doing more than wiring five code-review declarations. It makes
`_verifier_cfg`, the novelty pass's greedy verifier config, and the prerequisite ladder all take
effect for the first time.** That is the designed behaviour in every case — no code changed its
intent, only its efficacy — but it IS a live behaviour change to the plan-review gate, which is the
gate that reviews the plans in this very epic:
 * three Pass-2 sub-calls move frontier → the verifier model (with no class table configured, opus →
   sonnet). Intended and cheaper; the risk to weigh is that a sub-call which only reached its
   current verdict BECAUSE it ran on opus may now decide differently.
 * the prerequisite ladder starts actually escalating on context-limit errors, which changes what a
   large plan's prerequisite pass does under pressure (previously it retried the same model and,
   presumably, hit the same limit).

**FLAGGING RATHER THAN DECIDING.** Per the epic's mandate I am not calling any of this out of scope,
and I have not narrowed the fix to code-review to avoid the change — narrowing would leave four known
defects in place, and the epic's mandate is to ship WITHOUT BUGS. But "plan-review verifier passes
change model" is an operator-visible consequence of a story titled for code-review, so it should be
an explicit decision. If the operator wants the plan-review consequences verified before this lands,
the natural shape is a sibling ticket under 061c that re-runs a plan review and a prerequisite-heavy
plan under the new behaviour and records the observed per-pass models — which the Step 0 attribution
now makes checkable, and which was impossible before this ticket.

**Not cited as a defect, deliberately:** `resolve_verifier_model`'s equality rule remains superseded
and callerless per the standing decision. The live thing here is `_verifier_cfg`, which has callers.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ LIVE EVIDENCE: the declarations ARE honoured. This is the inverse of the original probe. ═══

A real `rebar review-code --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD` (attested source) on commit 2e17171e5c, from
the worktree build carrying the fix, with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` set and a **DISCRIMINATING** class table.

**THE TABLE MATTERS, and getting it wrong is why the original probe was ambiguous.** With no
`model_classes` configured, `frontier` resolves to the built-in `claude-opus-4-8` — which IS
`cfg.model` — so a frontier-declaring step runs on opus whether or not the declaration is honoured.
This run therefore made all three classes differ from `cfg.model`:
    cfg.model  = claude-opus-4-8      (the value a dropped declaration would fall through to)
    frontier   = claude-sonnet-4-6
    standard   = claude-haiku-4-5
So ANY opus row would prove a dropped declaration. There are none.

    step      op                                           model_class  model
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    base      code-review-base                             frontier     anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
    round_a   code-review-docs                             frontier     anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6

**AND EVERY ROW CARRIES `step` + `model_class` — Step 0 working in a real run.** Neither field

# Wire the model classes through the code-review gate (they are declared and ignored)

**Filed as a bug, RECLASSIFIED AS A STORY on operator direction: this is the epic's wiring work — carrying the three-class configuration through the review process — not a defect repair. The observable symptom below is what proves the wiring is absent.**

## Problem

`code-review.yaml` declares a model CLASS on all five of its LLM-calling steps, and **every one of
those declarations is silently ignored at runtime.** The gate runs every pass on the single resolved
`cfg.model`, which is exactly the one-knob behaviour epic 061c exists to remove.

MEASURED, not inferred. A real `rebar review-code` run with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` (one JSON record per
LLM call, written at the runner chokepoint `llm/runner.py:545`) under an INVERTED class config
(`frontier = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, `standard = anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`):

    1 code-review-base                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares frontier
    2 code-review-docs                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    3 code-review-tests                            anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    4 code-review-deletion-impact                  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    5 code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    6 code-review-api-compat                       anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    7 code-review-verify                            anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares standard
    8 code-review-coach                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares standard
    9 code-novelty                                  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8

Nine calls, all on the bare default. `verify` has declared `model: standard` since story 172e
closed, so **this is a pre-existing defect, not a regression** introduced by 3768.

## Three competing explanations; two eliminated by experiment

This is recorded because each cheaper probe produced the SAME observation, and only the discriminating
one settles it.

- **H3 — the class table falls back to built-in defaults** (the run is scoped to a snapshot read root
  via `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)`, so a config-file class table might not be visible).
  **ELIMINATED:** `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS['standard'] == 'claude-sonnet-4-6'`, so under H3 `verify`
  would have run on SONNET. It ran on OPUS.
- **H2 — the config pointer was never loaded.** **ELIMINATED:** with the same env var,
  `load_class_slots()` -> `resolve_class('frontier')` returns `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`,
  both with and without `repo_root=` (the form the gate uses).
- **H1 — the step's `model:` never reaches the resolver. CONFIRMED.** It is the only hypothesis that
  predicts opus for a step declaring `standard`. Corroborated directly:
  `resolve_model(cfg, step='frontier')` -> `bedrock:...` while `resolve_model(cfg, step=None)` ->
  `claude-opus-4-8`, which is precisely what was logged.

Also ruled out: the running package loads the worktree's own gate file with all five declarations
intact, and `code_review/shim.py:119 review_code` really does execute the gate via
`gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`.

## The lead: an asymmetry with the gate that DOES work

The plan-review gate honours classes — a live two-provider run showed a 41/1 opus/sonnet split across
providers. The dispatch paths differ in a way that is a concrete starting point rather than a guess:

- plan-review (`gate_dispatch.py` ~:146-163) wraps `run_workflow` in **`gate_config(cfg)`**, whose own
  comment says it "publishes `cfg` so every op (and the non-step ProductionBatchRunner) reads the SAME
  resolved config via `resolve_gate_config` instead of re-deriving from env".
- code-review (`gate_dispatch.py` ~:414-424) wraps only
  `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle), review_kernel.collect_contract_violations()` — **no
  `gate_config(cfg)`**.

Whether that omission is the cause or merely adjacent must be established before fixing; do not assume
it. `workflow/runs.py:154` does pass `step=ctx.step.get("model")` into `resolve_model`, and
`code_review/batch_runner.py:60-61,83-84` does resolve `req.model_ladder[0]` and set `step["model"]`,
so both halves look correct in isolation — the defect is in what actually executes for this gate.

## Approach

### STEP 0 (FIRST, and it is a deliverable in its own right): make the usage log able to attribute a call to a STEP.

`llm/usage_log.py` records `op=` — the PROMPT NAME — and nothing else that identifies the caller. That is why the nine-call log CANNOT locate this: `code-review-base` is the prompt used BOTH by the `base`
step AND as the `batch:` finder for `round_a`/`round_b`, so no observed record can be attributed to a
step. Diagnosing on top of that would mean guessing which path produced which call, and guessing from
an instrument that cannot see the distinction is how three earlier probes in this epic produced
confident wrong answers.

So the first change is OBSERVABILITY, not a fix: record the STEP ID (and the resolved model's declared
CLASS, when the value came from a class token) alongside `op` on every usage record. Properties this
must have: it is additive (existing consumers keep working — `summarize()` folds the file for
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`), it stays a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset, and it makes the CURRENT
defect visible as data rather than inference. Re-running the live probe after Step 0 is what turns
"nine calls on cfg.model" into "step X received model Y", which names the broken seam directly.

This also outlives the ticket: every future per-pass or per-provider question in this epic (0d76's
parity arms, eb6e's cutover, 8625's docs) needs exactly this attribution, and 0d76's own research
already assumes "the REBAR_USAGE_LOG rig records per-call model" — it records the model but not the
step, which is the half that matters for a per-PASS claim.

### Then the wiring

Diagnose first, then fix the narrowest seam. Trace one `base` call from `produce_code_review_verdict`
to the runner and identify where the declared class is dropped. Fix that seam so a declared class
reaches `resolve_model`/`resolve_model_string` for BOTH single-shot prompt steps and batch steps.

This ticket does NOT change any declaration in `code-review.yaml` — 3768 already made those correct,
and 172e's `verify` declaration is correct too. Only the plumbing changes.

## Scope

**STEP 0 — observability. These were previously listed in `file_impact` but NOT enumerated here; a
review round blocked four times on that single inconsistency, so they are spelled out.**

- `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` — **the primary Step 0 target.** Add the step id (and the declared
  CLASS when the model came from a class token) to what `record()` writes, and keep `summarize()`
  working on the new shape. `record()` must stay a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — **the only `usage_log.record()` call site, VERIFIED: `:547`**, called as
  `record(usage, op=_call_label, model=ran_model, provider=infer_provider(ran_model))`. `op` is derived
  from `_call_label`, which is why the log currently carries the PROMPT name and not the step.
  THE THREADING PROBLEM, stated because it is the real design decision in Step 0: `RunRequest`
  (`runner.py:~69`) has fields `system_prompt`, `instructions`, `config`, `reviewers`, `target`,
  `langfuse_prompt` — and **no step id**. So the step must reach `:547` by one of:
    (a) a new `RunRequest` field — explicit and typed, but touches every construction site;
    (b) the existing `target: dict` — no signature change, but overloads a field meaning something else;
    (c) a ContextVar set by the step executor and read at the record call — no signature churn, and it
        mirrors the existing precedent of `_active_gate_config` in `llm/config.py`.
  Pick ONE and record why; do not leave it to the implementer.

  **THE CLASS TOKEN HAS THE SAME PROBLEM, AND THE SAME ANSWER — carry BOTH on one mechanism.** By the
  time control reaches `:547` the class is GONE: `resolve_model()` has already collapsed the token to a
  model string, and `resolve_model_string()` (`model_classes.py:~264-287`) returns a bare string rather
  than a `(model, class)` pair. So the class cannot be recovered at the record call. But the RAW
  declared value is available at exactly the place the step id is — `ctx.step.get("model")` for a
  prompt step, `batch["model_ladder"][0]` for a batch step, i.e. BEFORE resolution. Whatever mechanism
  is chosen above to carry the step id must therefore carry that raw declared value alongside it, and
  `record()` stores it as the class when it is one of the reserved class names (`CLASS_NAMES`),
  otherwise omits it (a literal model id is not a class).
  **REJECTED — reverse lookup.** Deriving the class at `:547` by asking which class maps to the
  resolved model is not sound: two classes may legitimately resolve to the SAME model (e.g. an operator
  who points frontier and standard at one model), so the mapping is not invertible and the record would
  be silently wrong in exactly the configuration where per-pass attribution matters most.
  **REJECTED — changing `resolve_model_string`'s return type** to a tuple: it is called from several
  places for its string value, so widening the contract to serve logging would push churn across
  unrelated call sites for no behavioural gain.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — **NOT expected to change.** Named only to close the question: it
  emits the per-call caching warning that misled an earlier probe (it fires only when caching was
  requested and had no effect, so it captured 3 of 9 calls), but it does NOT call `usage_log.record`.
  If Step 0 turns out to need a change here, that is new information worth a comment.
  **DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM `file_impact`** — that field records files this ticket IMPACTS, and this
  one is named here only to close the question of whether it is involved. The asymmetry is intentional,
  not an oversight; every other file named in this Scope IS in `file_impact` (checked mechanically).

**THE WIRING FIX — the seam is NOT yet identified, and Step 0 exists to identify it.** Expect to change
ONE of these; do not change all three speculatively:
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — the code-review dispatch path (~:414-424), which omits the
  `gate_config(cfg)` scope the working plan-review path uses (~:146-163).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` — `RunnerAgentStep.run` (~:144-156) for single-shot prompt steps; it
  already reads `ctx.step.get("model")`, so if the drop is here it is upstream of this read.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` — `CodeReviewBatchRunner` (~:60-61, :83-84) for batch
  steps; it already resolves `model_ladder[0]` and sets `step["model"]`.

**READ ONLY:**
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the five declarations are already correct (3768 and
  172e) and MUST NOT change. If a fix appears to require editing them, the diagnosis is wrong.

- `tests/` — the usage-log attribution test and the end-to-end recording-runner test.


## Testing

**The missing test is the point of this ticket, not an afterthought.** 3768 shipped 9 tests and a 6/6
mutation score and STILL missed this, because every assertion checked either YAML content or
`resolve_model_string(<token>)` in isolation. Nothing observed the ENGINE PASSING the token to the
resolver, so no mutation could distinguish "declaration honoured" from "declaration ignored".

- END-TO-END, offline: execute the code-review gate with a RECORDING runner (a fake that captures the
  model it is handed per step) and assert each of the five steps receives its declared class. This is
  deterministic and free; it is strictly stronger than a live probe and it is the guard that would
  have caught this.
- the same test must FAIL on today's code — confirm RED before fixing.
- a mutation that removes the fix must break it (assert the anchor exists AND that the text changed;
  a mutation that silently no-ops looks identical to a test that cannot detect).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` record carries the STEP ID of the step that made the call, in addition to
      the existing `op` (prompt name). Asserted by a test that runs a gate with the log enabled and
      checks the recorded step ids — NOT by reading `usage_log.py`. Without this the log cannot
      distinguish the `base` step from the `round_a`/`round_b` batch finder, because both use the prompt
      `code-review-base`, and no per-PASS claim about this gate is checkable.
- [ ] a record whose model came from a CLASS token also carries that class, so a reader can tell
      "resolved to opus because frontier" from "resolved to opus because cfg.model" — the exact
      ambiguity that made three earlier probes in this epic unfalsifiable.
- [ ] the addition is ADDITIVE and inert when unconfigured: `summarize()` still folds a log written by
      the new writer, and `record()` remains a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset (asserted).
- [ ] [operator-attested] the live probe is RE-RUN after Step 0 and the resulting PER-STEP attribution
      is recorded in a comment — this is the DIAGNOSTIC run that names the broken seam, and it
      replaces inference with data. Tagged because it is an inherently external artifact (a live LLM
      run whose output is pasted into a comment) and the verifier cannot confirm it from code —
      exactly the untagged-external-evidence trap this epic has hit repeatedly.
      DISTINCT from the final live-run criterion below: this one runs on the BROKEN code to locate
      the seam; that one runs after the fix to show the declarations are honoured. Both are needed
      and neither substitutes for the other.

- [ ] an offline end-to-end test executes the code-review gate with a recording runner and asserts
      that EACH of the five LLM steps (`base`, `round_a`, `round_b`, `verify`, `coach`) receives its
      DECLARED class, not `cfg.model` — and it is observed RED on the pre-fix code
- [ ] the same test covers BOTH shapes: a single-shot prompt step (`base`, step-level `model:`) and a
      batch step (`round_a`, `batch.model_ladder`), because they travel different code paths
- [ ] a test asserts that under a class table whose values differ from `cfg.model`, NO step resolves
      to `cfg.model` — the assertion that discriminates "honoured" from "ignored"
- [ ] `verify`'s pre-existing `model: standard` (172e) is shown to be honoured by the same test, so
      this closes 172e's latent evidence gap rather than only 3768's
- [ ] no declaration in `code-review.yaml` is changed by this ticket
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real `rebar review-code` run with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` under a class table
      whose classes differ from `cfg.model` shows the per-pass model ids matching the declarations,
      cited from the JSONL in a comment — the run that currently DISPROVES the behaviour
